Subject: Recap + next steps from today's perf call (latency/throughput AB test)

Hi Ava / Tom —

Great to meet you both today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we covered:
- Scope: apples-to-apples latency & throughput comparison between Redwood (Redwood-2 family) and your current providers (Bedrock / Vertex) for the 13B-class workload you run in prod.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (inference throughput), and cost per 1M tokens under typical concurrency profiles.
- Test variants: cold-start vs warm-cache, seq lengths (128 & 2048), concurrency levels (1, 4, 8, 16).

Next actions we committed to: 
1) Redwood to run the AB test (full test plan attached: globex_benchmark_plan_v2.docx). We'll run on the same model family you use and a close Redwood equivalent (Redwood-2-13B quantized), and mirror your traffic patterns.
2) Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost estimate, and a short write-up with recommendations and suggested tuning (batching, KV caching, quantization). Target delivery: EOD Jul 22.
3) Follow-up review: 30-minute sync on Jul 23 to walk results and next steps.

Questions for you (if you can confirm in your reply):
- Which hyperscaler endpoint and model name should we compare against (exact Bedrock/Vertex model)?
- Any traffic shaping we should replicate (burst patterns, request size distribution)?

Attaching the test plan and our internal template. Sean / Marcus — please pick this up and coordinate the runs. Sean, can you own coordination with Globex? Marcus, SE to lead the runs and drop preliminary numbers.

Thanks —
Marissa
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Hyperscaler model: please compare directly to Bedrock's "xlarge-13b" endpoint (we've been using that). We can also add Vertex's "v-13b" if you want a three-way. Bedrock is priority.
- Traffic profile: 70% short requests (~60-150 tokens), 30% long (1000-2000 tokens). Burst windows ~ 30s every 5 minutes that spike concurrency to ~12-16.
- Cold vs warm: yes please include both. The p99 during bursts is what worries our SREs.

One ask: can you include tokens/sec normalized to a single GPU and also the end-to-end latency that a synchronous API customer would see? Also note our compliance team will want to see any data retention or logs behavior for the test traffic.

We can loop infra@globex.com into any test credentials you need (they prefer using ephemeral API keys). Looking forward to the deliverable on Jul 22.

—Ava
Ava Reynolds

Marcus / Sean — forwarding Globex clarifications. Please own the run and keep Ava / Tom in the loop. Important acceptance criteria and requirements: 

Run specifics we need to capture in the results: 
- Comparators: Redwood-2-13B (4-bit quantized) vs Bedrock xlarge-13b (their hosted). Optional: Vertex v-13b.
- Sequence lengths: 128 and 2048. Also include 60-150 token distribution as part of the mixed profile.
- Concurrency points: 1, 4, 8, 12, 16. Include burst pattern simulation (spike to 12-16 for 30s every 5m).
- Metrics: p50 / p95 / p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (aggregate and per-GPU), CPU/GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens (estimate).
- Warm vs cold: warm = primed KV cache and warmed kernels; cold = new process/container.
- Repeats: run at least 3 repeats per cell and report mean + stdev.
- Environment: use the same prompt set (see plan), deterministic RNG seeds where applicable, and record exact model config (quantization, batch size).

Deliverables: consolidated CSV (ab_test_results.csv), PDF summary (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_latency_report.pdf), and a short slide with recommended tuning knobs. Target EOD Jul 22 — please flag blockers early.

Marcus — can you start the runs today and share a quick internal status by EOD? Sean — coordinate keys / access with infra@globex.com and confirm whether we can use ephemeral keys.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — starting the runs now. Quick notes / assumptions before we run so results are interpretable: 

1) Warm vs cold definitions and measurement windows:
   - Cold: new process/container, zero priming, measure first 200 requests.
   - Warm: process warmed with 5x typical short requests + KV cache primed with a representative prefix set. Measure steady-state after a 60s warm period.

2) Batching and request shape:
   - We'll test with batch sizes [1, 4, 8] where supported; Redwood runtime will auto-batch but we'll enforce max batch to mirror Bedrock behavior.

3) Concurrency handling:
   - We'll run concurrency points [1,4,8,12,16]. For burst pattern we will run a 30s high-concurrency window every 5 minutes for a total of 30 minutes.

4) Metrics capture: tokens/sec will be reported both as aggregate across the cluster and normalized per-GPU. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency for end-to-end API (including queueing) and model-only decode latency where possible.

5) Cost calc: using your machine-type equivalent pricing for Bedrock and our Dedicated pricing model. This is an apples-to-apples estimate and will include GPU hours and amortized infra overhead.

I attached a short preliminary CSV with the first run (warm short-requests, concurrency 4) — numbers are preliminary and un-tuned. Notes from the run: Redwood-2-13B (quantized) shows ~18% better tokens/sec at concurrency 4 on short requests and stable p95 during bursts, but we see a small p99 tail during initial burst cold starts that we can mitigate with larger pre-warm. 

I'll continue runs overnight and post the consolidated CSV + PDF by Jul 22 as requested.

Attachments: ab_test_results.csv

—Marcus
